title: Call a function
summary: What happens when bytecode executes `OP_CALL`: `luaD_precall` builds a new `CallInfo` frame. A **Lua** callee is then run by the *same* `luaV_execute` C frame (no C recursion); a **C** callee is invoked immediately and its results are moved into place before `luaD_precall` returns. Calls made from C (`lua_call`/`lua_pcall`) enter through `ccall`, which uses the same `luaD_precall`.

title: Interpret bytecode
notes:
`OP_CALL A B C`: function in `R[A]`, `B-1` arguments (`B == 0`: up to `top`, set by the previous instruction), `C-1` results (`C == 0`: multiple). `savepc` is done before the call so errors report the right line.

The `startfunc`/`returning` labels reload `cl`, `k`, `pc` and `base` from the current `CallInfo`; that is what lets Lua→Lua calls and returns stay inside one C invocation.

title: Prepare a call frame
notes: Dispatches on the callee's type tag: `LUA_VLCL` (Lua closure), `LUA_VCCL` (C closure) or `LUA_VLCF` (light C function). Returns the new `CallInfo` for a Lua function and `NULL` for a C function (which has already run).

title: Resolve __call metamethod
notes: Shifts the callee and arguments up one slot and puts the `__call` handler in the function slot, so the original object becomes the first argument. Raises "attempt to call a X value" if there is none.

title: Ensure stack space (may run GC)
notes: Macro over `luaD_checkstackaux`. Because growing the stack **moves** it, the caller's `func` pointer is saved as an offset and restored afterwards — any other raw `StkId` held across this point is invalid. Runs `luaC_checkGC` only when it actually has to grow.

title: Grow the Lua stack
notes: Doubles the size (at least what was asked) up to `LUAI_MAXSTACK` (1,000,000 slots). Past the limit it reallocates to `ERRORSTACKSIZE` (200 extra slots so the error handler can run) and raises "stack overflow"; an overflow *while* handling that is `LUA_ERRERR`.

title: Reallocate and fix stack pointers
notes: Converts every pointer into the stack (`top`, open upvalues, each `CallInfo`'s `func`/`top`) to offsets, reallocs with **emergency GC disabled**, then converts back and sets `trap` in Lua frames so `luaV_execute` reloads `base`.

title: Push a CallInfo
notes: `CallInfo`s form a doubly linked list that is reused: `next_ci` takes `L->ci->next` if one exists and only allocates when the list is exhausted.

title: Call a C function
notes: Guarantees the C function `LUA_MINSTACK` (20) free slots, fires the call hook, then **releases the lock** (`lua_unlock`) around `(*f)(L)`. The C function returns how many values on top of the stack are its results.

title: C function (lua_CFunction)
notes: Library or host function such as `print` or `string.format`. It sees its arguments as stack indices 1..n and talks to the VM only through the C API.

title: Finish a call
notes: Fires the return hook, moves results down to where the function was (`ci->func`), then pops the frame (`L->ci = ci->previous`). `OP_RETURN0`/`OP_RETURN1` inline this when no hook is active.

title: Move results into place
notes: Fast paths for 0 and 1 wanted results; otherwise copies `min(nres, wanted)` values and pads with `nil`. With `LUA_MULTRET` all results are kept and `top` marks the count for the next instruction.

label: OP_CALL: set top to last arg, build callee frame
new frame, savedpc = first instruction
notes: Missing fixed parameters are filled with `nil` right after.

label: goto startfunc: run callee in this C frame
results to func slot, pad with nil
not CIST_FRESH: resume caller (goto returning)
notes: A frame marked `CIST_FRESH` was entered from C via `ccall`; there `luaV_execute` returns to its C caller instead.
